title: Fidelity Taxonomy & Scheduler Interop Matrix - operational manual
author: Lena Zhang
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines a pragmatic fidelity taxonomy (how we describe and measure request/response fidelity in the runtime), and a scheduler interoperability matrix that maps fidelity targets to scheduler behaviors and required telemetry hooks. It consolidates operational runbooks for diagnosing fidelity regressions, guidance for kernel scheduling policy authors, and benchmarking protocols used to validate fidelity-preserving changes.

Scope
- Applies to all inference traffic served by the runtime (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Focuses on single-request fidelity (decoding fidelity, model variant fidelity, prompt-preserve semantics) and cohort-level fidelity (consistency across canaries, shadow cohorts).
- Does not replace model-eval quality pipelines but complements them with runtime-level observability and mitigations.

Why this matters
- We often trade throughput/cost for fidelity. Without a shared vocabulary and clear scheduler contracts, teams make inconsistent changes that cause subtle quality regressions. This manual makes those tradeoffs explicit and operationally testable.

Definitions and fidelity levels
1) Fidelity levels (business-oriented):
   - FIDELITY:HIGH — Match-to-model output semantics; minimal decoding truncation, full KV cache warm, deterministic tokenization path, 99th-percentile quality invariants verified by shadow evals.
   - FIDELITY:STANDARD — Non-critical latency optimizations allowed (small batch fusion, soft-quantization fallbacks), acceptable for most consumer-facing services.
   - FIDELITY:ECONOMY — Aggressive cost controls (low-precision kernels, higher batching, prefix elision), intended for bulk processing where micro-quality differences are acceptable.
   - FIDELITY:BEST_EFFORT — Degraded mode used during capacity pressure or partial failure; best-effort fallback to compatible model variant with explicit response metadata.

2) Observability primitives (signals we require)
   - fidelity_label (string): One of the fidelity levels above (attached to request).
   - kernel_profile (string): Kernel variant used (e.g., stable-tc64, quant-r2).
   - kvcache_state (enum): warm|partial|cold.
   - decode_path_flags (set): includes token-truncation, temperature-clamp, sampling-mode.
   - quality_shadow_score (float): periodic shadow-eval score (0..1) when enabled.

Scheduler Interop Matrix (text table)
Columns: fidelity_label | admission_policy | kernel_preference | prefetch_hint | fallthrough_policy | telemetry_required
- FIDELITY:HIGH | strict admission (single-request slots) | prefer full-precision, deterministic kernels | pre-warm KV + prefix pin | fail open with immediate rollback to canary | kvcache_state, decode_path_flags, kernel_profile, quality_shadow_score
- FIDELITY:STANDARD | balanced admission (slot-sharing allowed) | mixed-precision allowed with quality gate | opportunistic prefetch | degrade-by-quantize w/ warning | kernel_profile, kvcache_state, admission_latency
- FIDELITY:ECONOMY | aggressive admission (batch aggregation, deferred slots) | prefer quantized/low-precision kernels | no prefetch, batch-prefetch only | fallback to cheaper model variant | kernel_profile, batch_size_histogram, cost_estimate_token
- FIDELITY:BEST_EFFORT | best-effort admission (background slots) | any compatible kernel | no prefetch | tag response with fidelity=best_effort and reason | kernel_profile, eviction_events, failure_cause

Scheduling policy author guidance
- Always declare a fidelity_label at route definition. Default = FIDELITY:STANDARD.
- Keep scheduler policy small and declarative. Example policy snippet (YAML):

  route: /v1/generate/summary
  fidelity: FIDELITY:HIGH
  admission:
    mode: isolated
    max_concurrency: 4
  kernel_preferences:
    - stable-tc64
    - stable-tc32
  prefetch: true
  fallthrough:
    - route: /v1/generate/summary-lite
      fidelity: FIDELITY:STANDARD
      probability: 0.05

- Policies must include an explicit fallback route or fallthrough policy when the chosen kernel or capacity is unavailable.
- When adding a new kernel variant, update the interop matrix and include a microbenchmark that exercises the fidelity-sensitive prompt set.

Profiling playbook for fidelity regressions
1) Rapid triage (0–15 min)
   1. Isolate affected routes by checking fidelity_label in recent traces.
   2. Pull kernel_profile and kvcache_state histograms for the route over the last 60 minutes.
   3. If quality_shadow_score dropped >5% vs baseline, open a P0 incident and attach the shadow-eval corpus.

2) Deeper investigation (15–180 min)
   1. Run a targeted synthetic replay of failing prompts against the candidate kernel variants using the replay harness.
   2. Compare decoding artifacts: tokenization diffs, truncation flags, and final-length distributions.
   3. Check scheduler admission logs for unusual batching or coalescing events.

3) Remediation (post 3 hours)
   1. If a kernel regression is responsible, roll kernel to previous stable via the kernel-rollout tool and execute canary smoke checks.
   2. If admission policy caused harmful batching, temporarily tighten admission mode for the route and schedule a follow-up to analyze long-term capacity.
   3. Apply a temporary traffic-split to route a small percentage to a high-fidelity variant while investigation continues.

Runbook: canonical commands and scripts
- Pull recent traces for route: curl -s "${CONSOLE_URL}/api/traces?route=/v1/generate/summary&from=-1h" | jq .
- Kernel histogram: runtime-admin kernel-histogram --route=/v1/generate/summary --window=60m
- Launch replay job (isolated): replay-runner --corpus=shadow/summary-failures.jsonl --kernel=stable-tc64 --parallel=4
- Set temporary admission override: schedulerctl set-admission --route=/v1/generate/summary --mode=isolated --reason="fidelity-regression-20250318"

Benchmarking and validation protocol
- For every scheduler-change that may affect batching/admission, run the fidelity-preservation benchmark suite:
  1. Prompt sets: prod-top-1000, adversarial-250, stress-long-seqs-200.
  2. Metrics to collect: mean quality_shadow_score, 95th decode-time, token-length-distribution, perplexity-delta vs gold-model.
  3. Pass criteria: quality_shadow_score within 1.5% of baseline for HIGH/STD; within 6% for ECONOMY.
  4. Use controlled concurrency and live traffic shadowing (0% traffic injection initially).

Compatibility & preflight checklist for kernel rollouts
- Update kernel_profile registry with metadata: precision, determinism, known-issues.
- Create a perf matrix: (kernel x route) with expected throughput and latency delta.
- Add observability hooks if missing: ensure kvcache_state and decode_path_flags are emitted by kernel adapter.
- Run the benchmark protocol above and document the pass/fail outcome in the rollout ticket.

Telemetry contract (minimum required fields)
- trace_id (string)
- timestamp (iso8601)
- route (string)
- fidelity_label (string)
- kernel_profile (string)
- kvcache_state (string)
- batch_size (int)
- admission_mode (string)
- quality_shadow_score (float, optional)
- failure_cause (string, optional)

Escalation and ownership
- First responder: runtime-oncall (primary).
- Secondary: kernel-team (kernel regressions), serving-runtime (scheduling/telemetry gaps), ml-evals (shadow-eval gating).
- When to escalate to engineering leadership: any fidelity_shadow_score drop >10% affecting >5% of requests or undiagnosed degradation >6 hours.

Implementation examples (JSON policy + telemetry example)
- Scheduler policy (JSON example):
  {
    "route": "/v1/generate/summary",
    "fidelity": "FIDELITY:HIGH",
    "admission": {"mode": "isolated", "max_concurrency": 4},
    "kernel_preferences": ["stable-tc64", "stable-tc32"],
    "prefetch": true
  }

- Telemetry sample (single-line JSON event):
  {
    "trace_id": "t-0a1b2c3d",
    "timestamp": "2025-03-18T14:22:30Z",
    "route": "/v1/generate/summary",
    "fidelity_label": "FIDELITY:HIGH",
    "kernel_profile": "stable-tc64",
    "kvcache_state": "warm",
    "batch_size": 1,
    "admission_mode": "isolated",
    "quality_shadow_score": 0.987
  }

Operational examples & anti-patterns
- Anti-pattern: declaring fidelity=HIGH but leaving prefetch=false and admission=shared. This creates a latent mismatch where kernels assume warm cache but scheduler does not.
- Anti-pattern: using BEST_EFFORT for user-facing routes without response metadata. Always surface degraded-fidelity reasons in response headers: X-Redwood-Fidelity: best_effort; X-Redwood-Fidelity-Reason: kernel-eviction.

Notes for product and SRE collaborations
- Product must provide an explicit fidelity SLA when requesting high-fidelity routes (e.g., SLO: maintain quality_shadow_score above 0.95 at 99th percentile).
- SRE will verify observability hooks exist before approving kernel or scheduler policy changes. Any missing telemetry is a blocker.

Appendix: small checklist for reviewers
- [ ] Does the route declare fidelity_label?
- [ ] Are fallthroughs defined for capacity or kernel failure?
- [ ] Are required telemetry fields emitted for this route?
- [ ] Has the prompt set been added to the fidelity benchmark corpus?
- [ ] Are canary and shadow strategies defined for rollout?
